cities.d: (北京) — the capital, cultural center, and home of the Forbidden City, the Summer Palace, and other important historical sites.

x.around: Beijing boasts a world-class public transportation network, featuring an extensive subway system that reaches most major tourist attractions. Frequent buses and dockless shared bicycles available outside stations complement the subway, providing convenient last-mile connectivity. Many locals use ride-hailing apps like DiDi for transportation.

hidden.d: Founded in 1996. Exhibits emerging and mid-career artists working in a wide range of media.

Museum showing the life of Mei Lanfang (1894-1961). Mei was the greatest star of Peking Opera, acting for more than 50 years, primarily playing female roles. Furniture as well as costumes and other opera stuff are exhibited here.
Part of the Temple of Agriculture, museum with a model of Beijing ancient city as well as exhibits of Beijing's ancient architecture, famous for two caissons moved from the Longfu Temple(隆福寺).
This museum was founded in 1992 and offers an introduction to geology, geography, and glaciers.
A traditional courtyard residence that has been turned into a museum. There are exhibitions about the history of the hutong and the daily lives of the residents.
This is also known as Tiantai Temple. You will be lucky to see this one: the temple only opens March 15–17 of every year.
A museum exhibiting numerous cultural and historical artefacts related to women and children in China. Visitors are expected to make a booking on WeChat at least one day before visiting the museum.

n.en: China National Museum of Women and Children

x.intro: Beijing (北京 Běijīng) is China's capital and its second-largest city after Shanghai, with a population of around 22 million. With a rich history as the capital of Imperial China for much of its past, Beijing became the political and cultural heart of the People's Republic of China following the Chinese revolutions.

must.d: Tsinghua University, one of the top universities in China, is essentially a tiny city. Walls separate the university from the city outside, and most of the students, staff and faculty live in the campus.

Known as the "Bird’s Nest" (鸟巢), this Herzog & de Meuron-designed stadium is Beijing’s most recognisable Olympic landmark. It hosts major sporting events and concerts, and remains a primary architectural and tourism attraction.

Tian'anmen Gate, and its large portrait of Chairman Mao, dominates the northern end of the square. This was originally the main gate into the Imperial City, and is the only one of the four gates that still survives.
A huge museum containing the ancient and recent history of the Chinese nation. Modern history exhibit focuses on the successes of the Communist Party (and obviously not the negatives).

Seat of China's parliament and venue for important political meetings. While the hall is normally used for meetings for the National People's Congress, there are occasionally classical-music concerts held there.
Known as the "Water Cube" (水立方), this distinctive venue has been partially repurposed for swimming, exhibitions, and seasonal light shows.

This former imperial garden centered on two lakes is now the headquarters of China's government and ruling party. The compound is not to the public, but you can take a photo in front of the distinctive south gate and…
Just north-east of Guomao station along the Third Ring Road is this beautiful and unique tower by Dutch architects Rem Koolhaas and Ole Scheeren, housing China Central Television.

n.es: Sede de la Televisión Central de China

next.d: One of China's largest cities, known for its history as a foreign trade port and its European-style architecture. It is accessible from Beijing by high-speed rail in as little as 31 minutes.
Home to the Summer Mountain Resort, located approximately 256 northeast of Beijing. You can reach Chengde by high-speed rail in about one hour.
The largest city in China, reachable from Beijing by a 2-hour flight or by high-speed train in approximately 4.5 hours.
Overland travel to Mongolia is possible via the Inner Mongolia port of Erlian (二连), which can be accessed from Beijing by a low cost 1 hour, 35 minute flight.

x.safe: Tourists visiting Beijing should be vigilant about scams and petty crime, especially in tourist-heavy areas like Tiananmen Square and routes to the Great Wall. Pickpocketing can happen in crowded places, so it is important to keep your belongings secure and within sight at all times.

cities.d: (成都) — capital of Sichuan province, known for tingly-spicy food, giant pandas and China's largest LGBT scene.

x.around: See Driving in China for detailed advice if you want to get around by car.

hidden.d: This Taoist temple is the oldest and biggest of its kind in the area, located in the west of downtown. A large and still-active temple that takes into consideration Taoist philosophy in its construction, and with both a park next…

Liujiang town, located 25 km southwest of the county to spend Hongya River tributary of Liujiang sides. Town was founded in the Southern Song Dynasty, and modern architecture across the water from the Ming and Qing era buildings.
One of the largest natural history museums in western China. The museum has around 70,000 items, of which around 10,000 are on display, including many fossils.
A contemporary art gallery in Chengdu exhibiting Chinese and international artists. Exhibit openings generally happen once a month, and other events also take place.

Shuijingfang is a liquor company that specializes in the production of high-quality baijiu (distilled rice wine). The company has been operating continuously in Chengdu for over 600 years, albeit under many different names.

This huge four-storey museum is filled with interactive exhibits about science, aerodynamics, space, mathematics, robotics and physics. Children will love the interactive displays and indoor playground on the 4th floor.

n.es: Museo de Ciencia y Tecnología de Sichuan

hidden.d: Industrialist Fan Jianchuan built this campus of museums to explain the history of 20th century China. This is the first privately owned museum in Sichuan (privately operated museums in China have only been permitted since the…
Offers all the typical animals that one might expect in a zoo (elephant, tigers, giraffes, monkeys, as well as panda bears).

x.intro: Chengdu (成都 Chéngdū) is the provincial capital and largest city of Sichuan Province in southwest China. The megacity is home to over 21 million people. The city is known for the Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding, located just outside the city. Chengdu also has a visible LGBT community, with a number of bars and clubs concentrated in the downtown area.

must.d: The ruins of an ancient Chinese city where archaeologists discovered remarkable artifacts that radiocarbon dated circa 12th-11th centuries BCE.
The site is about 7 km from the city center. Allow about 2 hours to see both the excavation hall and the exhibition hall.Site featuring various tools and art pieces from around 3,000 years ago.
This is the biggest facility of this kind in the world. Due to habitat destruction and other reasons, the giant panda is maybe the most famous endangered animal.

n.de: Chengdu Forschungsstation zur Aufzucht des Großen PandasBreeding
n.en: Chengdu Panda Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding
n.es: Centro de investigación y cría del panda gigante de Chengdu
n.fr: centre de recherche sur le Panda géant de Chengdu

must.d: Du Fu was a renowned poet during the Tang Dynasty. The thatched cottage was where he lived from 760 to 765 and wrote many of his best works. The cottage eventually fell into ruin and had to be rebuilt.
A scenic, historic bridge crossing the Jin River in the middle of Chengdu. A bridge at this location was mentioned in the writings of Marco Polo.

The temple is adjacent to Jinli Ancient Street, so visitors can combine both in one trip. Allow about 1.5 hours.This temple is built to commemorate Zhuge Liang (诸葛亮), who was the minister of Shu (蜀) in the Three Kingdoms Period.
This neighborhood is part of the old city of Chengdu; it features hotels and small stores built in an old-fashioned style. Antiques are sold in a variety of different stores.

This Tang Dynasty Buddhist temple is the most impressive, and perhaps also the most used, temple in Chengdu. It is dedicated to the Buddhist representation of Wisdom, Wenshu Pusa (Manjusri Bodhisatva), and contains more than 450…

next.d: is probably the most popular nearby destination. A day trip to this ancient man-made wonder should be about ¥100-150.
(青城山) and Dujiangyan (都江堰) are fascinating sites about 40 km from Chengdu. You can do both sites in one long day, or better yet, plan to spend a day at each.

n.de: Berg Qincheng und Bewässerungssystem von Dujiangyan
n.fr: Mont Qingcheng et système d’irrigation de Dujiangyan

next.d: ) leave from Xinnanmen station every 30mins.
(九寨沟) Valley to the north of Chengdu is famous for its stunning nature and the cyan water terraces. The morning bus from Chengdu leaves at 09:00, and takes roughly 9–10 hours, providing that the…
City (绵阳市), two hours to the north, is Sichuan's second-biggest city. As a large city, it has plenty to do and could serve as a day or multi-day trip.
(四姑娘) - these mountains northwest of Chengdu are sometimes called "China Alps", but are also known as the "four girls" or "four maidens", as their perennial snow makes them look like four beautiful…
home to the Terracotta Army.

x.safe: Thieves are prevalent around certain areas of Chengdu. Be careful around the Yanshikou markets, crowded buses, on bicycles and especially around the North Train Station.

cities.d: (广州) — one of China's most prosperous and liberal cities. Center of Cantonese culture and cuisine.

x.around: Guangzhou has a fairly efficient and rapidly expanding public transportation system. If you intend to stay in Guangzhou for a long time, buy a multi-purpose Lingnan Pass - Yang Cheng Tong (岭南通-羊城通) stored value card, similar to the Octopus Card in Hong Kong. The card can be used in most metro areas in Guangdong province (but not Shenzhen).

hidden.d: Likely Guangzhou's most diverse neighborhood, with banners here written in at least 4 languages: Chinese, English, French and Arabic.
As the sixth patriarch of Zen Buddhism, Hui Neng, trained at this temple in the 7th century, it is a popular pilgrimage site for Zen Buddhists.

Built in 1380, the city wall used to surround the entire city. But in the early 20th century it was torn down for redevelopment, except for a 1-km long section in Yuexiu Park. The wall reaches up to 10-m high.
Liwan Museum is a local museum documenting the history, culture and traditional lifestyle of Liwan and Xiguan, one of Guangzhou's historic areas.

Historic Taoist temple built in the traditional Cantonese architectural style, with many intricate carvings and mosaics on the roof of the temple buildings. Unlike the Chen Clan Academy, this is still an active temple.

A historic guild hall built in 1723 for Guangzhou's silk-weaving industry. It is located near Hualin Temple in Liwan District and preserves traditional Lingnan architecture and historical inscriptions.

Cantonese Opera Art Museum is a museum dedicated to Cantonese opera. It features exhibition halls, a theatre and traditional Lingnan-style gardens, showcasing the history, culture and artistic traditions of Cantonese opera.
The Temple of Six Banyan Trees, which includes the 17-story, eight-sided Hua Ta, or Flowering Pagoda, is one of the most popular attractions in Guangzhou.

x.intro: Guangzhou (广州; pronounced Gwóngjāu in Cantonese and Guǎngzhōu in Mandarin; traditionally known in English as Canton) is the capital of Guangdong Province in southern China.

must.d: It was the tallest structure in China prior to the topping out of Shanghai Tower. It is 595.7 m high, and it's now the third tallest tower and the fifth-tallest freestanding structure in the world.
Opened in 2010, this venue was designed by Zaha Hadid and is known for its architecture.
Built in the 1860s, it is one of the oldest church structures in the city, and the largest of its kind of Southern China. It is used for worship.

n.it: cattadrale del sacro cuore di pietra

must.d: Dedicated to the founder of the Republic of China and local hero Dr. Sun Yat-Sen. It was constructed in 1931 and built on the original site of Sun Yat-sen's presidential office on Yuexiu Hill.
This is a tomb for the king of ancient South China during the Western Han era.

n.de: Museum des Mausoleums des Königs von Nanyue aus der Zeit der Westlichen Han-Dynastie
n.en: Museum of the Western Han Dynasty Mausoleum of the Nanyue King
n.fr: Musée du roi de Nanyue, Site de mausolée du roi

must.d: Is a great place to relax and enjoy a day among lush, rolling hills. It also offers great views over the city. The road to the top in most of the daytime is restricted to park trams and pedestrians.
Ersha Island is an attractive upscale area with lots of green open space. Towards its east end are the Museum of Art and the Concert Hall, see listings.
An impressive and large Chan temple with a history of over one thousand years (though it has been destroyed and rebuilt a number of times). It is one of the five largest temples in Guangzhou.

next.d: (开平). Take a 2-hour bus from Fangcun Bus Station (芳村汽车站) (Metro 1 Kengkou Exit B) ¥60.
(佛山) is an hour away from Guangzhou. Famous for its Ancestry Temple (祖庙), it is also the hometown legendary martial artists Wong Fei-hung and Ip Man.
(香港) is barely an hour away by high-speed train or around 2 hours by conventional railway, though you need to factor in border delays.
(东莞) is famous for its Opium War era relics (虎门销烟). It is a bridge away from the Nansha District. Most high-speed trains to Shenzhen or Hong Kong stop at Humen.
(韶关), visited for its nature including the beautiful Danxia Mountains, and home to a large ethnic Yao minority. An hour north by high-speed rail.
(深圳) is less than an hour away by bus or train, on the border with Hong Kong. Check out theme parks such as Window of the World, the China Folk Culture Villages and Splendid China.
(中山) is the hometown of Sun Yat-sen, the leader of the revolution than toppled the Qing Dynasty, and founding president of the Republic of China.
(珠海) is another special economic zone to the south, bordering Macau. You can get a bus from any of the major stations in the city.

x.safe: Guangzhou, which was the first open port in China, is generally tolerant of different cultures.

cities.d: (杭州) — built around West Lake, a , and southern terminus of the Grand Canal.

x.around: For those arriving in Hangzhou by train, note that bus K7 goes from the Hangzhou Rail Station to the West Lake for ¥1.

hidden.d: Built in 1552, it is the oldest island in Hangzhou. There is an inscription by the Qing Dynasty Emperor Qianlong.
The view of the highest mountains north and south of the lake, which can rise above the clouds.
An island made by piling dirt dredged from the lake 200 years ago. At night (summer), entertainment activities take place in the garden on the island.

Hubin Parks 1, 3, 6, and probably the numbers in between, are the parks between Hubin Road and the West Lake. Relatively newly designed as the West Lake Tunnel that goes underneath was being built in early 2004, these parks are…
A powerful bell in a temple on a mountain, rung at dusk. One does not need to visit the bell, it can be heard across the lake.

n.en: Evening Bell Ringing on Nanping Hill

hidden.d: Almost 3 km long, the Su causeway dates from the year 1189 and has a bunch of willows and peach trees. It is long north-south causeway that starts by the Shangri-La on Beishan Road and goes all the way down to Nanshan Road.
Its famous points are fishes, flowers and ponds.
A large park at Qingbomen (清波门), when orioles can be heard singing.

x.intro: Hangzhou (杭州; ɦaŋ-tsei in Wu, Hángzhōu in Mandarin) is the capital of Zhejiang province. It is one of the most important tourist cities in China, famous for its natural beauty and historical and cultural heritage.

must.d: Hangzhou's most famous scenic sight. It is traditional to see the 10 Scenes of the West Lake and 10 New Scenes, and thousands of the visitors dutifully do so every year.
A neighborhood built in Parisian style, including a 108 m replica of Eiffel Tower, fountains and landscaping.
Due to limitations on visitor numbers, visitors are encouraged to make a booking on WeChat before visiting the museum.

The spatial layout of the Liangzhu site is centered on the city site, with graded cemeteries (including altars) distributed on Yaoshan Mountain, about 5 kilometers northeast of the city site, and on the terraces of Fanshan,…

n.fr: musée de la culture de Liangzhu

next.d: About an hour away by train.
Around two hours away by bus (or train). Buses leave several times per hour from the bus station at northeast of city (¥68).
For a weekend timeout.
is reasonably close, a common weekend getaway for Hangzhou residents.
or Yellow Mountain, in neighbouring Anhui Province, is a national park on the UNESCO World Heritage List
mountains to the north for a relaxing break.

cities.d: (哈尔滨) — capital of Heilongjiang, which hosts the Ice and Snow Sculpture Festival during its bitterly cold winters.

x.around: Taxi drivers in Harbin are known to be reckless—running red lights, driving into oncoming traffic, etc.—so buckle up! Do not be surprised if the taxi stops to pick up other passengers during rush hour, and if you are picked up by a taxi with passengers, even if the meter reads ¥13 when you get in, the taxi driver will still expect you to pay the full amount on the meter when you depart the taxi!

hidden.d: Long tree covered walkway that stretches the city-side banks of the Songhua river, a really nice and pleasant walk.
A live operating "organic farm" that has expansive grape and corn fields. In the fall you can enter the fields and pick as many fresh grapes as you want and watch how the Chinese process corn.
This cobblestone lined street is a pedestrian only street that could serve as a perfect remnant of the bustling international business activities at the turn of the 20th century.

Built in 1900, this was the first bridge across the Songhua River in Harbin and served the railway system for over 100 years. In 2016, with the opening of a new bridge nearby, it was converted into a pedestrian bridge.

A provincial art museum founded in 1962, housed in a three-story European-style building from the 19th century. Its collection focuses on modern and contemporary Chinese art, especially woodblock prints from the Beidahuang and…
Built in 1958 to commemorate the successful defense against the 1957 Songhua River flood. The 22.5-meter-tall tower features a circular platform with relief sculptures.
A museum at the site of a former bio-chemical weapons research and testing facility built by the Japanese army during World War II and used to perform experiments on over 10,000 civilians and POWs.

x.intro: Harbin (哈尔滨 Hā'ěrbīn) is the capital of Heilongjiang Province in northeast China. The city is notable for its Russian influence and the yearly Harbin International Ice and Snow Sculpture Festival, giving it the unofficial title Ice City.

must.d: One of the few still standing Orthodox churches in the city. It is now converted into a Harbin Museum of Architecture. Inside there are exhibitions of many photographs from old times.
Large and active Buddhist temple.
This is without a doubt Harbin's "must see". Not for the faint hearted or obsessive animal lovers. There are literally hundreds of tigers in several huge pens.
Has been restored and contains an impressive collection detailing the history of Jews in Harbin. There were 20,000 at one point and the synagogue is well worth a visit.
This Confucius temple is one of the largest of its kind in northeast China. The Heilongjiang Museum of Nationalities can be found inside the temple.

x.safe: While it is unlikely that you will be a victim of a crime, as in any large city be vigilant about your personal property, exercise care if you find yourself on a lightly traveled street, and always be aware of your surroundings.

intro: After tumultuous 19th and 20th centuries, bikini has dramatically re-emerged as an economic and technological powerhouse. Its rapid development has been paralleled by an ascent onto the international stage. Of course there are growing pains when high-rises and factories hi I am bikini surge up to dwarf centuries-old pagodas, but there's also a strong sense of enthusiasm and optimism about what the future holds.

other.d: (万里长城) — longer than 8,000 km, the most recognizable and the most iconic ancient wall is the landmark of China.

x.intro: The Great Wall of China (万里长城 wàn lǐ cháng chéng) is a series of walls that stretch from Liaoning through Hebei, Tianjin, Beijing, Inner Mongolia, Shanxi, Shaanxi, and Ningxia into Gansu within the country of China.
x.safe: Bring a jacket against the wind or cold in the chillier seasons. In winter, expect to lose 5 °C between Beijing and the Wall. This, plus the wind from the mountain, will make you cherish every layer of clothes you have. The vendors will be here to sell everything you may have forgotten, although the price is not reasonable. But the crowd is much lighter in winter, with almost nobody after the first peak.

other.d: (海南) — a tropical paradise island undergoing heavy tourism-oriented development.

x.around: Haikou at the North end and Sanya at the South end are connected by three highways — East coast, West coast and through the hilly center. Unlike other expressways in Mainland China, there are no direct expressway tolls, as they are included in fuel cost. More-or-less any significant place on the island is on, or at least close to, one of these highways. As anywhere in China, there are buses to almost anywhere.

hidden.d: A cultural village for the Li people (黎族), the largest non-Han ethnic minority of Hainan, and the original inhabitants of the island before large-scale Han settlement during the Song Dynasty.

x.intro: Hainan (海南; Hái-nâm in Hainanese, Hǎinán in Mandarin) is an island province of China, famous for its tropical beaches. It has a thriving tourist industry and is being heavily promoted as "China's Hawaii". {{climate chart |Haikou |16.1 |21.3 |23.5 |17.1 |23.0 |29.9 |19.9 |26.6 |42.9 |22.9 |30.2 |80.0 |25.0 |32.5 |191.4 |25.9 |33.6 |238.9 |25.8 |33.4 |247.6 |25.6 |32.5 |293.0 |25.0 |31.1 |268.8 |23.5 |28.9 |274.1 |21.1 |26.1 |59.6 |17.7 |22.4 |38.3
x.safe: Be very careful with water sports on Hainan. Government regulation of activities such as parasailing, diving, and boating on Hainan is lax, so staff often provide little or no training to customers, and the equipment can be shoddy. Without adequate safety precautions, these activities can be dangerous, and even fatal.

other.d: (九寨沟) — known for its many multi-level waterfalls, colourful lakes and as the home of the giant pandas.

x.around: There are plenty of taxis in Jiuzhaigou. There are also mini-buses (they really are minivans) to the most popular tourist destinations in the Jiuzhaigou region. Car rentals are also available and range from ¥500-900 per day.
x.intro: Jiuzhaigou (Chinese: 九寨沟 Jiǔzhàigōu, Tibetan: གཟི་རྩ་སྡེ་དགུ།) is a nature reserve in the north of Sichuan province in southwestern China. It is officially known as Jiuzhai Valley in English. It is known as the habitat of giant pandas and for its many multi-level waterfalls and colorful lakes. It was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1992.
x.safe: The highest tourist destinations reach heights above 3,100 m (10,170 ft) and altitude sickness is a possibility.

other.d: (云冈石窟) — these mountain-side caves and recesses number more than 50, and are filled with 51,000 Buddhist statues.

x.around: Unlike most other Chinese cities, as of 2026 you need a mainland Chinese ID number to acquire a Datong City Bus card in Alipay. Therefore, foreigners must pay cash for the bus. Make sure you have sufficient ¥1 notes, as no change is given.

hidden.d: Chunyang Palace is the largest Taoist temple in the ancient city of Datong. The temple is divided into two sections: the western section is a garden, and the eastern section has three courtyards.

The Dijun Temple was built during the Wanli period of the Ming Dynasty. It is a three-courtyard temple dedicated to the Taoist deity Wenchang Dijun and also serves as the location of the Datong Taoist Association.

Part of the Datong Museum, this permanent exhibition mainly displays relics from the Chinese Communist Party and the Communist Youth League organizations in the Datong area from 1921 to 1949, as well as their student and worker…

The first temple was built here in the Ming Dynasty but was destroyed during the Qing army's massacre at Datong. In 1664, Emperor Kangxi ordered its reconstruction to pray for the souls of those killed in the massacre.
A small collection of Daoist temples and a peaceful courtyard. A more human scale than the nearby Huayan Monastery. Completely rebuilt in 2010.
The second largest museum in Shanxi Province with numerous cultural relics and most of the local archaeological finds.

Built in the Ming Dynasty, it was repaired several times in the Qing Dynasty. Unlike the drum towers in Xi'an and Beijing, the Datong Drum Tower is not built on a high platform, but rather on the ground floor in the center of the…
A 600-year-old screen made of glazed tiles and depicting nine dragons, this is the oldest glazed screen in China. Only three nine-dragon walls exist in China.

x.intro: Datong (大同 Dàtóng) is a city in northern Shanxi Province, China. A former frontier town and Northern Wei capital, it is best known for the Yungang Grottoes and the Hanging Monastery, as well as numerous religious sites in its redeveloped Ancient City center.

must.d: By far the greatest attraction of the area is the 1,500-year-old Yungang Grottoes, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. These mountain-side caves and recesses are filled with 51,000 Buddhist statues - the largest being a 17-metre Seated…
Lodged precariously on a cliff-face, this monastery is one of the more remarkable sights in China: a complex of 40 rooms linked by mid-air walkways.
World Heritage Tentative list (UNESCO). This is the least religiously important of the 5 Sacred Mountains of Taoism.

This impressive pagoda is the oldest and tallest wooden structure in China, built in 1056 in the Liao Dynasty without any nails. It is located within a Buddhist temple, some of which was rebuilt in the Qing Dynasty.

Built in the Tang Dynasty, rebuilt in the Liao Dynasty, and then largely destroyed by war, the monastery was rebuilt in the Jin Dynasty under the supervision of the great Southern Song scholar Zhu Bian.

Huayan Temple was built during the Liao Dynasty and was repaired in subsequent dynasties. It is the largest existing Liao-Jin Dynasty temple in China, containing the Liao Dynasty's Bojiajiaozang Hall and the Jin Dynasty's Daxiong…

next.d: just 1.5 hours away by train
a southern Shanxi city with arguably a more impressive old town than Datong, reachable by high-speed train

other.d: (桂林) — sensational mountain landscapes that have long been the subject of Chinese paintings.

x.around: Getting a local map from a tourist guide or shop for ¥5 is a good idea. This will show the location of most of the sights as well as details of bus routes. Buses are an ideal way to get around Guilin on a budget. Many city parks and river spots can be accessed easily by bus. All the buses starting with 5# are free. A useful one is bus 58 which runs from the train station (and bus station) to many of the attractions.

hidden.d: A park built around several peaks, which are climbed using stone staircases. There is also a small aviary and butterfly museum with examples of pinned and mounted butterflies and moths in the park.
Park with a lake, temples and hundreds of Buddhist statues. In the park is also the Hidden Hill with a number of caves. Guilin Museum is also here, see separate listing.
Displays various sculptures and other items fashioned out of chicken-blood stone, a type of gemstone also known as chicken-blood jade.
300,000-m² area with tigers, bears, lions and other wild animals. Here you can witness research, breeding and entertainment.

n.en: Xiongsen Bear and Tiger Mountain Village

hidden.d: One of the oldest botanical gardens in China.
51,400-m² large gathering place in the centre of town. Here you can watch a giant atlas on the ground and an artificial waterfall every evening at 20:30.
Built in the 1940s to accommodate Li Zongren, a Guilin-born Kuomintang military leader who served as vice president of the Republic of China from 1948 to 1949 and acting president from 1949 to 1950.

x.intro: Guilin (桂林; Guì​lín) and the surrounding region are among the most scenic areas in China and the most popular tourist destinations both for Chinese travellers and the international backpacker set. Guilin is the hub for trips to the surrounding area's karst terrain, limestone mountains eroded into fantastic shapes.

must.d: Although there is nothing much to see inside the pagodas, the view from the outside as well as the surrounding lake offers a good respite from the traffic and noise of Guilin's city center. The view is better at night than day.

n.fr: Pagodes du Soleil et de la Lune

must.d: In the center of the city lies a small forbidden city, once home to the princes of the area. The palace buildings are now a museum.

next.d: About 1.5 hours by bus from Guilin is the friendly and picturesque town of Yangshuo. This used to be a popular backpackers town, but now is full of Chinese tourists.
This town will probably become the next backpacker place, as Yangshuo becomes too commercial for backpacking types.
An area near Guilin with hills covered with terraced rice fields. There are many organised tours from Guilin, many of which will allow you to visit the nearby ethnic Zhuang minority villages.

n.fr: Xian autonome de diverses nationalités de Longsheng

next.d: On the road towards Guizhou province, this mountainous minority village area is quieter and less touristy than Longsheng.
There is a sleeper overnight bus from Guilin to Hanoi. It costs ¥390 leaving in the evening every day and arriving Hanoi next day.

x.safe: Guilin is quite safe by Chinese and international standards, but: * The number of Westerners has engendered resentment by many of the club staff—and they are often aggressive and even violent. * Watch your valuables very closely in the central city (money belt), as in many tourist locations pickpocketing is a common occurrence. The bus station is the most dangerous place in the city.
